I'd suggest short id of `OGL-Canada-2.0` or `OGL-CA-2.0`. C alone isn't very meaningful, and it is version 2.0. 😄

sorry, forgot the `2.0`!

And agree re `OGL-C-2.0` not being meaningful. Finding more references to `OGL-Canada-2.0`:

https://enterprise.dejacode.com/licenses/?q=open+government
https://github.com/okfn/licenses/blob/master/licenses/OGL-Canada-2.0.json

https://enterprise.dejacode.com/licenses/?q=open+government

This license is only usable by "Her Majesty the Queen in right of Canada ", e.g.  the government of Canada.  So unless this the license text is templatized, this is a single user license.

I suggest a scoped license identifier of LicenseRef-.gc.ca.-OGL-2.0

@mlinksva you wrote:

> I'd suggest short id of OGL-Canada-2.0 or OGL-CA-2.0. C alone isn't very meaningful, and it is version 2.0.

... and I second this. FWIW I have opted for a slightly different key in ScanCode:
https://github.com/nexB/scancode-toolkit/blob/develop/src/licensedcode/data/licenses/can-ogl-2.0-en.yml
to group together each of the provincial or city variants with the same prefix:
https://github.com/nexB/scancode-toolkit/blob/develop/src/licensedcode/data/licenses/can-ogl-alberta-2.1.yml
https://github.com/nexB/scancode-toolkit/blob/develop/src/licensedcode/data/licenses/can-ogl-toronto-1.0.yml
https://github.com/nexB/scancode-toolkit/blob/develop/src/licensedcode/data/licenses/can-ogl-toronto-1.0.yml
https://github.com/nexB/scancode-toolkit/blob/develop/src/licensedcode/data/licenses/can-ogl-alberta-2.1.yml

@swinslow it is widely used -- this is the primary license structure for open data in Canada.

There are at least 10,000 datasets here.

https://open.canada.ca/en/search/inventory

For a more specific example, it's used by Natural Resources Canada (think the USGS)
https://www.nrcan.gc.ca/earth-sciences/geography/topographic-information/licence/17285

As @pombredanne notes, there are many provincial and city variants.

https://vancouver.ca/your-government/open-data-catalogue.aspx

Very similar wording in the Statistics Canada data licensing 

https://www.statcan.gc.ca/eng/reference/licence
https://www.statcan.gc.ca/eng/reference/licence-faq

Given the wide usage that @burritojustice noted in the first link from the preceding comment, I believe that this should be added to the list. 

(I haven't compared it to the provincial / city / Statistics Canada variants that are noted separately -- if those are substantively different licenses under the [SPDX matching guidelines](https://spdx.org/spdx-license-list/matching-guidelines), then those wouldn't fall under this entry.)

I'll raise this on the legal team call today for others' input, but my view is that it is appropriate to add.
Ok to add, and we can always consider in the future to add markup text if and in order to accommodate different entities using the same license
